Embed a plot as HTML in a knitted Quarto or R Markdown document

Source: R/cnvs-embed.R
cnvs_embed.Rd

A convenience wrapper around cnvs() for embedding plots directly in a knitted document that already produces HTML output. Rather than opening the device yourself and remembering to call grDevices::dev.off() and standalone = FALSE, cnvs_embed() does all of that around a single plotting expression and hands back an object that knitr will drop into the document verbatim (via knitr::asis_output()) – no results: "asis" chunk option needed.

Usage

cnvs_embed(expr, width = 480, height = 480, pointsize = 12, bg = "white")

Arguments

expr

A plotting expression, e.g. plot(1:10) or print(ggplot2::ggplot(...)). Evaluated with the cnvs() device active, so ordinary base or grid plotting calls work as they would in any other chunk.

width, height

Device size, in pixels (used directly as the width/height attributes of the <canvas> element).

pointsize

The default font pointsize, in big points (1/72 inch), following the same convention as grDevices::pdf() and friends.

bg

Default background colour, as a colour name or other value accepted by grDevices::col2rgb().

Value

An object of class "knit_asis" (as produced by knitr::asis_output()) wrapping the <canvas>/<script> HTML for the plot. Auto-printing this at the top level of an R chunk is enough for knitr to insert the raw HTML into the rendered document.

Details

Internally, this writes to a temporary file exactly the way cnvs() always has (there is no in-memory buffering mode – see the discussion of this tradeoff in the package's design notes); the file is read back in and deleted once its contents have been captured. Each call gets its own cnvs() id_prefix, derived from the temporary filename R already guarantees is unique, so calling cnvs_embed() from several chunks of the same document never produces clashing <canvas> ids.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  out <- cnvs_embed(plot(1:10, main = "cnvs_embed() demo"))
  class(out)
}
#> [1] "knit_asis"
